invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.
Every changed page keeps working without JavaScript; JavaScript only enhances it (conflicts:c-006).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).
'Save and return to overview' saves without the page's required-answer checks, but still refuses an answer that fails its own format rule (conflicts:c-211; ruling:sam-2026-10-07).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.title: Commodity details asks germinal products for gross weight, packages and storage temperature
increments.detail: Germinal products are counted by weight and packages, not by animals. On Commodity details each germinal species asks 'Total gross weight' in kg and 'Number of packages', both required; a germinal-only consignment also asks one storage 'Temperature'. A germinal commodity has one Selected commodities row listing its species. The gross weight is stored per species and passed on as the consignment's gross weight, the error summary orders errors by question, and the overview's Commodity details task completes only when every germinal answer is valid.
acceptanceCriteria: Each germinal-product species asks 'Total gross weight' in a narrow input with the suffix 'kg'; left blank it shows 'Enter the total gross weight', and anything but a number above 0 with an optional decimal part shows 'Enter a number greater than 0', each linked to that field. increments.title: Main import reason completes on its own answers, and both pages soft-save as Design Release 2.1 does
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 judges the main import reason task on the reason's own answers, with Additional details its own task. An answer that breaks its own format rule, such as an impossible exit date, is still refused, because the service cannot store it.

Such a notification never sees the additional details page: its certification purpose is set to 'Germinal products' automatically and shown on the review without a Change link. A mix of live animals and germinal products keeps the full lists and the page.

The real frontend offers no germinal-product commodity today, so this row needs the commodities area's rows that add germinal products to the commodity search (req-092, req-093): the combiner should make it depend on them. increments.title: Arrival details page moves to the 'arrival-details' address
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 names the arrival details page by what it asks. Today it is served at .../port-of-entry. After this change the page is served at .../arrival-details, and every link into it from the overview and the review goes there, so the address a trader sees matches the page.

increments.title: Arrival details wording: labels, hints, placeholder and means of transport options
increments.detail: Bring the arrival details page's visible copy up to Design Release 2.1: medium-size question labels, the new port of entry hint and placeholder, the shorter means of transport options and the shorter transport identification lead-in. increments.title: Arrival details requires a means of transport, and arrival and transit return to where the trader came from
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 makes means of transport the one required answer on arrival details, because it decides whether transit countries are asked. It also sends a trader back to where they started: the overview when they opened the page from the overview, the review when they came from the review. 'Save and return to overview' lets a trader leave a part-finished page without a means of transport. The real service keeps every field check it has today (c-045): a page with any error saves nothing and shows the entries back, and an answer that cannot be stored, such as an impossible date, is refused even on 'Save and return to overview' (c-211).
acceptanceCriteria: Save and continue on arrival details with no means of transport chosen stays on the page and shows 'Select a means of transport to the port of entry' in the error summary, linking to the means of transport select, and above the select, which is shown in its error style (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-039, prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-040; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p8-030, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p8-031)
When that error shows, the page title starts 'Error: ', nothing is saved and the other answers entered are shown back (conflict c-006; conflict c-045)

When arrival details was opened from the overview's 'Arrival details' task, Save and continue with valid answers saves them and returns to the overview (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-012, prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-053)

When transit countries was opened from the overview's 'Transit countries' task, Save and continue saves the countries and returns to the overview (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-067; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p11-099)

When arrival details was reached from the page before it in the journey, Save and continue still goes on to transit countries for Rail or Road and to Transporter details otherwise (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p11-052; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p10-028)

When arrival details was opened from a Change link on the notification review, Save and continue saves and returns to the review (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-053, prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-083)

'Save and return to overview' on arrival details with no means of transport chosen saves the other answers, raises no error and goes to the overview, where 'Arrival details' is not Complete (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-051; conflict c-211)

'Save and return to overview' on arrival details with an impossible arrival date, such as 31 2 2027, stays on the page with 'Enter a real arrival date' and saves nothing (conflict c-211; conflict c-045; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p11-019)

'Save and return to overview' on transit countries saves the countries listed and goes to the overview (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-080; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p17-059)
notes: Combines req-315 (means of transport required), req-327 (return to overview), req-328 (return to review) and req-329 (Save and return to overview): all four decide what Save and continue and Save and return do on the same two pages, and each criterion needs the others' set-up to observe. c-045 keeps today's field checks, so the prototype's soft-validation claims are not built; c-211 keeps format checks on 'Save and return to overview'. Where the journey-flow area builds a general 'return to where you came from' mechanism, the combiner should make this row depend on it rather than build a second one. The flow files are shared.

increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 names the page 'Transit countries' in the browser tab, steps Back to arrival details when the trader came from there, hides the list until a country is added, and sends anyone who opens the page when the means of transport is not overland back to the overview.

Opening the transit countries page's address when the saved means of transport is Air or Sea, or none is saved, goes to the overview (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-060; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-088; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p8-042)

increments.title: Transit countries are added and removed in place with JavaScript, with 'Added' and 'Removed' announcements
increments.detail: With JavaScript, Design Release 2.1 adds a country as soon as it is picked and removes one without a page load. increments.title: Document references accept punctuation, and the document type list drops Health certificate

increments.title: Upload documents remembers where the trader came from and returns them there
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 carries where the trader came from (the overview or the review page) through every reload of the page, so its Back link and Save and continue return the trader where they started, and otherwise Save and continue goes to the next journey step, Consignment addresses. c-transporters-001 (default): with JavaScript the form opens with its address and contact fields hidden behind the search and 'Enter address manually'; without JavaScript the address and contact fields show from the start. Follow the default unless it is answered otherwise.
notes: Combines the search (req-456), filling the fields from the chosen address (req-457) and the fields hidden behind the search until revealed (req-458): one widget.

Combiner, after the reconciler settled req-456 and req-457: unblocked. c-218's default makes the Northern Ireland search observable in the fit suites and on the local stack by giving the lookup stubs BT addresses (the stack's simulator lives in trade-imports-stub, so the stub repo joins this row and the envelope), and c-217's default gives CDP test, ext-test, perf-test and prod the form with every field shown and no search. The INS backend serves the lookup; it is in repos in case the animals frontend needs access to it. Adding a client-side script needs its build entry, or it 404s silently.

increments.title: Identification details takes its place in the linear journey after Commodity details
increments.detail: DR2.1 runs the journey page to page: Commodity details continues to Identification details when a selected species has identifier fields, Back returns to Commodity details, and Save and continue moves on to the next journey page. Today the page is reached only from the Overview task row, its Back link and Save and continue both go to the Overview, and a direct visit with nothing to identify lands on the Overview. Afterwards the page is a real journey step that is skipped when there is nothing to identify, while the hub, review and template-review entry points keep returning where they came from.

increments.title: Each species panel saves only its own animal, with the saved-animals table below the form
increments.detail: DR2.1 saves a multi-animal species one animal at a time through its own panel button, and the page's own buttons save only species with one animal. Today any save, the page's Save and continue included, validates every card and appends a record for every card that holds data, so one card's failure can leave earlier cards' records saved. DR2.1 also puts the saved-animals table under the form, shows only the table once every animal is entered (no completion message), and makes the panel button primary.

increments.detail: Today the hub's Identification details row shows Complete straight after Commodity details, before any animal is identified, and stays Complete at 1 of 2. DR2.1 counts identification complete only when every animal of every selected species with identifier fields has a complete entry. For submitting, DR2.1 makes identification optional for a single species but needs at least one complete entry per species when more than one species is selected; the identification page itself shows no message for that rule.

increments.title: A permanent address page for cats, dogs and ferrets, with one card per animal and a same-as-destination choice
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks for each pet's permanent address on its own page in the consignment parties section, opened from the consignment addresses page, instead of inside the animal identification form. The page has a card for each cat, dog or ferret (not other live mammals), showing the identifiers already given, and asks for each one whether the animal lives at the place of destination or at a new address, revealing the address fields only when a new address is chosen. Each animal's choice and address are stored with the notification, every field in its own place, and a trader can save what they know and come back.
acceptanceCriteria: A consignment with cats, dogs or ferrets has a 'Permanent address' section on the consignment addresses page explaining 'A permanent address is where an animal:' with the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address' to the permanent address page; for cats alone there is no CPH section (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-023, p9-025; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-085, p7-106; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-081)

A consignment of other live mammals alone has no permanent address section, and opening the permanent address page for it sends the trader to the consignment addresses page (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-023, p9-024; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-109)

The permanent address page has the caption 'Consignment parties', the heading 'Permanent address', the browser title 'Permanent address - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and a back link to the consignment addresses page (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-021, p9-032, p9-033; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-109, p13-110; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-082, p3-108)
The animal identification page no longer asks for any address field (document:dr1-parity-backlog p6-058; trace:e2e p6-028)

The page shows one card for each animal that needs a permanent address, as many as were entered for each species, headed with the scientific name and a running number such as 'Felis catus 1'; species that do not need one get no card (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-037, p9-038; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-091, p13-111; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-084)

Each card shows the animal's entered identifiers in inset text as 'label: value', such as 'Microchip: MICROCHIP-1', leaving out blank ones, and shows no inset when none are entered (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-039; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-111)

Each card asks 'Select an address' with the options 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' and 'Enter a new address', neither chosen when the page first opens; once a place of destination is given, the first option's hint is that address on one line, such as 'Riverside Holding Facility, East Farm Road, Leeds, LS25 3EB, United Kingdom' (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-040, p9-041, p9-042; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-092, p7-094, p7-095, p13-112; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-085)

'Enter a new address' has the hint 'This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination.', and choosing it reveals that animal's own address fields inside its card, with 'Email address' before 'Phone number' (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-042, p9-043, p9-050, p9-051; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-093, p7-097, p7-098; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-086, p3-090)
The page ends with the 'Save and continue' button alone, which saves and returns to the consignment addresses page (document:dr1-parity-notes p1-055, p1-056, p1-058; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-104)

An animal saved as 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' carries the place of destination's name, address, country, email and phone as its permanent address; reopening the page shows that option selected (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-067, p9-068; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-115)

A new address saved with a county and no address line 2 reopens with 'Enter a new address' selected, each value in its own field: the county in 'County', the town in 'Town or city' and the postcode in 'Postcode or Zip code', with country United Kingdom (ruling:sam-2026-10-07 p1-010; prototype:dr2-1-source p9-068; trace:e2e p6-032)

An animal left with no option chosen raises no error: the page saves the other animals and returns to the consignment addresses page, and the permanent address section stays incomplete, holding the notification back from submission, until every animal that needs one has an address with a name (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-062, p9-063, p9-074; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-102; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-089)

increments.title: The address book record carries what an address can be used for
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 records what each address can be used for (its uses), and the first use gives the address its primary type and the address book tab it sits on. Today the address-book record is untyped and its API carries no type or use, so nothing can keep the answer to the add form's uses question, and the address book list's category tabs and the DR1 address pickers have nothing to filter on. Conflict c-address-book-add-and-edit-001 settles it: the record and its create, read-one and update API gain the address's uses, and the 'untyped and unroled' ruling cv-044 is set aside. Afterwards an API caller can create, read and update an address with its uses, and addresses saved before the change still read back, with no uses.
acceptanceCriteria: Creating an address through the address book API with one or more uses (place of origin, consignor, place of destination, consignee, importer, branch address) stores them, and reading the address back by id returns the same uses in the order given, the first being the address's primary type (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-079; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-081; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-137; repo:addressbook p1-096)
Updating an address through the API with a different set of uses replaces its uses with the new set, and the read-back shows the new set (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-079; repo:addressbook p2-071)

A create or update carrying a use outside those six is refused with a 400 validation problem whose errors name the uses field, and nothing is saved (repo:addressbook p1-039, p1-045; prototype:dr2-1-source p16-079)
An address created without uses, and every address saved before this change, is still accepted and reads back with no uses (repo:addressbook p1-001, p1-003)
A request carrying a stray 'type' or 'role' field is still refused with a 400, as today (repo:addressbook p1-038, p2-016; c-address-book-add-and-edit-001)

The address book's locked API contract describes the uses field on the create and update requests and on the read response, with its six allowed values (repo:addressbook p2-097, p2-098; document:dr1-parity-backlog p7-064, p7-065)
increments.gate: Check the uses field's wire name, its six values and how a missing field reads back in the locked contract before the add form, the address book list's category tabs and Type filter (address-book-list area) and the DR1 address pickers build on it.
notes: Pass 1 slice on its own: the typed record is the foundation the add form's uses question (this area), the list's category tabs and Type filter (req-address-book-list-016 to 023) and DR1 inc-047/inc-048 all rest on, so it lands first and gates. Observable through the API in every environment the tests repo's address book API client reaches (local stack and CDP). Uses stay optional on the API so a notification journey's add (today's handshake, req-address-book-add-and-edit-093, still a question) and every existing record keep saving; the add form makes a use required outside a journey (row 'Saving a new address with its uses'). Updates fully replace the editable fields today (req-073), so the edit page must post the stored uses back; that is the edit row's criterion. Decision: refuse an unknown use with a 400, because the record only means something with known values (validation clause of ruling:sam-2026-10-07).

increments.title: Adding an address starts by choosing its type

increments.title: Saving a new address with its uses
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks what an address can be used for on the add-details step and saves the ticked uses with it, then shows the user the new address among its kind. Afterwards an Origin or Consignor address offers 'Place of origin' and 'Consignor' after a section break, a use is required once the fields are valid, the save stores the ticked uses in the address book, and the user lands on the list's tab for that type, with the new address first, a reworded success banner, its full address and searchable by its uses.
acceptanceCriteria: For 'Origin or Consignor' the address and contact fields show straight away with no address search, then a section break, then the uses question with the legend 'What can this address be used for?', the hint 'Select where this address can be used' and the checkboxes 'Place of origin' and 'Consignor', with no hint on either option (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-025, p16-048, p16-052, p16-053, p16-054, p16-055; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-054, p16-065, p16-066; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-119, p6-120)

With the address and contact fields valid and no use ticked, saving shows 'Select what this address can be used for' inline and in the error summary, linked to the first use option; while any field is invalid the uses are not checked (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-076; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-077, p16-129; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-135)

Saving stores the address in the address book with every ticked use, and a use posted that does not belong to the chosen type is not stored (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-078, p16-079; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-056-m1, p16-081)

After saving an Origin or Consignor address the user lands on the address book at /address-book?category=origin-and-consignor, with the new address listed first and a 'View' link to its own page (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-083, p16-086; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-079, p16-081, p16-082; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-137, p6-139)
The list then shows a 'Success' banner reading '<name> address added to your address book' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-085; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-080)

The added address reads as address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county and postcode joined by commas, leaving out blanks, with the country shown separately (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-080, p15-084; trace:ins-fit p1-058)
The added address is found by the address book search on its name, on a use label such as 'Consignor', on part of its address and on its country (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-082)

increments.title: Destination, Consignee or Importer and Branch addresses: search first, manual entry and a fixed UK country

acceptanceCriteria: In the fit suites, on the local stack and in CDP dev, for 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' the add-details step opens with only the address search; the address fields, contact fields and uses question stay hidden until an address is picked or manual entry is chosen, and open already revealed when an address or address line 1 is already present (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-025, p16-037; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-083, p16-096, p16-098; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-140, p6-141; conflicts:c-217)

For these two types the uses question's legend is 'Address type' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-052; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-095, p16-099)

A 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' address offers the use checkboxes 'Place of destination', 'Consignee' and 'Importer' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-056; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-097; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-144)

Saving with nothing picked or typed shows the six field errors with the address and contact fields revealed, so each error summary link moves to a visible field; the errors stay until the next save, and the typed values, ticked uses and search text are kept (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-077; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-092, p16-094; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-142; repo:insfrontend p3-065; c-address-book-add-and-edit-005)

In CDP test, ext-test, perf-test and prod, where no address lookup is set up, the 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' add-details step shows no address search and no 'Enter address manually' button, and opens with the address and contact fields and the uses question shown, as the 'Origin or Consignor' step does; every field, message and save is the same as elsewhere (conflicts:c-217)

increments.title: The address search finds UK addresses as you type
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1's search is a free-text type-ahead that fills the address from a picked result. The prototype searches made-up data shipped with the page; c-address-book-add-and-edit-003 rules the real service searches real addresses through the address lookup the INS backend already serves (GET /address-lookup with find=<term>), with the INS frontend's stub in stub mode. Afterwards typing in 'Search for an address' lists matching addresses; picking one fills address line 1, address line 2, town or city and postcode, with United Kingdom; name, email and phone stay for the user; a failed lookup still leaves manual entry.
acceptanceCriteria: The address search is a text field labelled 'Search for an address' with the placeholder 'Start typing...' and an icon button whose accessible name is 'Search' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-026, p16-027; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-084; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-140)

Typing in the field lists matching addresses below it in a list labelled 'Address search results', each shown as the lookup's formatted address line with the typed text in bold, and a screen-reader announcement gives the number of results, such as '3 results available' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-027, p16-029, p16-030; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-086, p16-086-m1; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-143; c-address-book-add-and-edit-003)

Picking a result hides the search, announces 'Selected <the result's address>' to screen readers and reveals the fields filled from it: premises to address line 1, street and locality to address line 2, town to town or city, the postcode, and country United Kingdom; name, email address and phone number stay blank, and anything the user types over a filled field is what is saved (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-033, p16-034, p16-035; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-087, p16-088, p16-089; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-145; repo:insfrontend p5-052 to p5-059; c-address-book-add-and-edit-003)

In stub mode and on the local stack, a search lists the lookup stub's London addresses, among them '1 DOWNING STREET, LONDON, SW1A 1AA', and picking it fills address line 1 '1 DOWNING STREET', town or city 'LONDON' and postcode 'SW1A 1AA' (repo:insfrontend p5-073 to p5-079; c-address-book-add-and-edit-003)
In the CDP dev environment, searching a real UK postcode or street lists real addresses from the address lookup (repo:insfrontend p5-067, p5-069; c-address-book-add-and-edit-003)
In CDP test, ext-test, perf-test and prod the add-details step shows no address search, and the address is entered by hand in the fields it opens with (conflicts:c-217)

Where the search runs, when the lookup fails or finds nothing no results are listed and 'Enter address manually' still reveals the fields, so the address can be entered and saved by hand (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-028; repo:insfrontend p5-070, p5-071)

increments.title: Editing an address matches Design Release 2.1
increments.detail: The edit page takes Design Release 2.1's heading, field order, layout and country select, returns the user to where they came from on Back and Cancel, keeps every use the address has, words its success banner as Design Release 2.1 does, and sends the user back rather than to an error page for an address not in their book. Today the heading is 'Edit address details', Phone comes before Email, the fields use other widths, the country select keeps a placeholder, Back and Cancel ignore any return path, and unknown ids show page not found.

increments.title: Destination-side journey add pages find UK addresses by search

The address book returns an organisation's addresses for one requested role in a single unpaginated list, carrying each record's roles, and never returns a deleted record (document:dr1-parity-notes document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-022, document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-023; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-050, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-052)

In stub mode, each picker lists only the canned records that carry its role, so the five pickers do not all list the same addresses (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-168, repo-frontend-p9-169, repo-frontend-p9-170)

Each picker lists every address it offers on one page, with no pagination links, however many addresses the role has (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-052, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-056, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-057)

With JavaScript, typing in the search box hides, without a page reload, every row whose name, address lines and country do not contain the typed text in any case, and the results count updates to match (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-057; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-074 to trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-076; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-054)

The picker shows no 'Selected address:' inset; a party's chosen address shows as its checked row when the picker is reopened (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-050, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-055)

sources.ref: document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-047 to p6-056, p7-049 to p7-057

increments.gate: Look at role filtering on the compose stack and in stub mode before the rows that rest on it build: a role-carrying record appears only on its roles' pickers, a record with no role appears on all five, the list is one page, and the live filter and the no-JavaScript search both narrow it. The same-as row and the place of origin country search build on this.
notes: Combines role filtering (address book roles and role-scoped list, the animals frontend asking by role, untyped fallback, stub roles) with one-page listing, the live filter and dropping the 'Selected address' inset, because c-094 rules they land together: one page is only sensible once it is one role's addresses, and the inset only existed to carry a selection across pages. c-100: DR1's typed-record block is lifted; the typed record is built here in trade-imports-address-book. c-101: untyped records show on every picker until given a role, in the compose stack and CDP alike, never filtered on a guess. The animals frontend's address-book service stays read-only (c-106). Giving a record its roles through the INS address book's add and edit pages belongs to the address-book-add-and-edit and party-address-add-and-edit areas; on the compose stack the role-carrying records these criteria use are set-up for a one-page assertion through the address book, which the test rules allow, so this row does not wait for those pages. The tests repo's pagination and later-page-selection tests (repo-tests-p5-013, p5-018, p5-020) change with it.

increments.title: Same-as shortcuts on the roles and addresses page
increments.detail: Lets a trader fill the consignor from the place of origin, and the importer and place of destination from the consignee, with one button press on the roles and addresses page, as Design Release 2.1 draws. The button copies the source party's record onto the notification as an independent copy, so a later change to the source does not ripple through.
acceptanceCriteria: With a place of origin chosen and no consignor, the Consignor row shows a 'Same as place of origin' button styled as a link beside 'Add a consignor' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-033; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-042; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-049)

With a consignee chosen and no importer, the Importer row shows a 'Same as consignee' button styled as a link beside 'Add an importer'; with a consignee chosen and no place of destination, the Place of destination row shows a 'Same as consignee' button beside 'Add a place of destination' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-034; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-043, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-044; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-050)

No same-as button shows while its source party is empty or its target party already has an address, and no other pair of parties offers one (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-049, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-050; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-038)

Pressing a same-as button reloads the roles and addresses page with no success banner, the target row showing the source party's name and full address with a 'Change' link and no same-as button (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-035, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-036; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-045 to trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-048; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-051)

After copying, changing the source party to a different address leaves the copied target party's address as it was (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-037; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-052; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-021)

The copy is made even when the source address does not carry the target party's role, and the target party then shows that address (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-037; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-099)

The copied party carries the source's name, address lines, country and contact details through to check your answers (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-036; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-085, repo-frontend-p9-086)

The same-as buttons work with JavaScript turned off, and every new string has a Welsh machine-draft counterpart (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-023; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-089)
notes: Combines the three same-as buttons and their shared show and copy rules: one page form, one copy behaviour, one set of tests. c-100: DR1's collision block does not hold this back. Today the summary list sits outside the page's form (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-023), so the buttons need the form around them. Order: build after the roles and addresses page copy row (it asserts the full address and the named add links) and after the role-filtered pickers row (the 'copy even when the target's picker would not offer it' criterion needs role-carrying records). On the compose stack the role-carrying record for that criterion is set-up for a one-page assertion, allowed by the test rules.

increments.title: Place of origin picker searches by country
increments.detail: Gives the place of origin picker the country search Design Release 2.1 draws: its own label, hint and placeholder, and a country autocomplete that keeps the rows in the chosen country. Without JavaScript, submitting a country narrows the list on the server.
acceptanceCriteria: The place of origin picker's search is labelled 'Enter a country' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-054; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-072; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-035)

Its hint reads 'Enter each country that the consignment will travel through' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-054; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-127, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-103)
Its search box shows the placeholder 'Search for a country' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-054; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-072)

With JavaScript, typing offers country suggestions and keeps only the rows whose country contains the typed text; picking a suggestion keeps only the rows in exactly that country; clearing the box shows every row again (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-055; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-073, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-101, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-096)
Without JavaScript, submitting a country narrows the list to addresses in that country (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-054)
The other four pickers keep their 'Search' label and free-text search, and every new string has a Welsh machine-draft counterpart (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-053, repo-frontend-p9-089)
notes: Combines the place of origin picker's label, hint, placeholder and country filter: one picker, one search control. c-102: adopted as the prototype draws it, though the hint reads like transit-country copy; no DR1 judgement or constraint overrides it. Order: build after the role-filtered pickers row, whose live filter and one-page list this country filter builds on, and after the picker layout row, which reshapes the search control.

increments.title: Picker 'View' link to the INS address book and back
increments.detail: Replaces each picker row's in-place 'View details' expander with a 'View' link that opens the address in the INS address book, and makes the INS address book bring the trader back to the same picker. The INS frontend stays the one place an address is shown in full.
acceptanceCriteria: Each picker row ends with a 'View' link, and there is no 'View details' expander (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-062; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-060)

On the compose stack, following 'View' opens that address in the INS address book, and its back control returns the trader to the same party picker of the same notification (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-061; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-062)
The 'View' link has a Welsh machine-draft counterpart (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-089)
notes: Kept apart: it is the area's only change to the INS frontend and carries a cross-service return path the others do not. c-097: the prototype wins; the INS frontend must honour the return path, and the tests repo's in-place expander test (repo-tests-p5-014) changes with it. In stub mode, where no INS frontend runs, the fit suite observes the link's presence only; where it leads is observed on the compose stack. The builder should accept only a return path inside the animals journey, as the INS add handshake already does (journey-registry), so the link is no open redirect; this is a safeguard, not a source requirement, so it is left out of the acceptance criteria.

increments.title: The CPH number page follows Design Release 2.1: who is asked, its help and hint, a blank save, and where it goes
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks for a county parish holding (CPH) number for every live animal kept on a holding, not only today's list, and lets every commodity code but the pet, horse and germinal-cattle codes in. The page's help gains a second place to find the number, the hint loses its punctuation, the boxes stop browsers offering saved values and bring up the digit keypad, and a trader can save the page blank and move on, with the gap held at submission instead. The page is a step of the consignment addresses section: it is opened from that page and always returns to it. Every changed English string gets its Welsh machine draft in the same change.
acceptanceCriteria: A consignment holding cattle, ornamental fish, pigs, sheep, goats, chickens, turkeys, ducks, geese, guinea fowl, rabbits, camels, ostriches, parrots, reptiles or bees is asked for a CPH number; one holding only horses, cats, dogs, ferrets, other live mammals, cattle semen (05111000) or cattle embryos/ova (05119985) is not, and its consignment addresses page has no CPH section (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-001, p9-002; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-106; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-110; trace:e2e p6-068, p6-070)
Opening the CPH number page for a consignment the question does not apply to sends the trader to the consignment addresses page (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-001; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-106)

The CPH help's second paragraph reads 'You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK.', with 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' a link to https://www.gov.uk/guidance/get-a-county-parish-holding-cph-number (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-009 cph-number.html:50; trace:animals-fit p13-018; trace:e2e p6-084)

The CPH question's hint reads 'For example 12/345/6789', with no comma and no full stop, and still describes the whole group of three boxes (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-010; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-119; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-040; trace:animals-fit p13-007)

Each of the three CPH boxes turns browser autocomplete off and asks for the digit keypad, with the pattern [0-9]* alongside the numeric input mode (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-012; trace:animals-fit p13-014)

Saving the CPH page with all three boxes empty shows no error: any saved CPH number is cleared, the trader returns to the consignment addresses page, the CPH section there stays incomplete, and the notification cannot be submitted until a number is added (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-014, p9-015, p9-004, p8-135)

The CPH page's back link goes to the consignment addresses page however the page was reached (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-021; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-117; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-043; trace:e2e p6-078)

'Save and continue' with a valid CPH number saves it and returns to the consignment addresses page, never on to the contact address page or the notification overview (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-018; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-045; trace:e2e p6-074)

With the Welsh language chosen, the changed help paragraph and hint show in Welsh, marked as a machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off (repo:frontend p10-050, p10-051, p10-052, p10-053)
notes: Combines the CPH page's applicability (req-699), copy (req-706, req-708), box attributes (req-710), blank save (req-714, c-113) and navigation (req-719, req-720, c-115): all one page, one review. The Welsh rule req-725 sits here but covers the permanent address and contact rows too; each of those rows carries its own Welsh criterion. The combiner may prefer req-725 as an envelope invariant.
Conflicts followed: c-113 (a blank save moves on, with no error), c-115 (back and continue always to the addresses page), c-117 (GOV.UK guidance URL in place of the prototype's '#').

Depends on the commodities area's catalogue rows (req-093 germinal products, req-094 pigs to bees, req-099 ferret and other live mammals, req-100 ornamental fish): the first criterion names commodities today's five-commodity stub catalogue lacks. The combiner wires that dependsOn. The exempt list grows from codes 0101 and 01061900 to add 05111000 and 05119985.
The stored CPH number stays nine bare digits (c-112); only the display changes, in the addresses-page row.

increments.title: The consignment addresses page shows the CPH number as 12/345/6789 and continues to the contact address
increments.detail: On the consignment addresses page the empty CPH row's bare 'Add' becomes the link 'Add a CPH number', and a saved number reads in the slashed county/parish/holding form traders know, on that page and on the review page. 'Save and continue' on the addresses page moves on to the contact address page whether or not the CPH number applies: the CPH page is one of the addresses page's sections, reached from its own link, not a step after it.
acceptanceCriteria: Before a CPH number is saved, the consignment addresses page's 'County parish holding (CPH) number' section, after the place of destination, offers the link 'Add a CPH number' to the CPH page (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-003; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-038; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p12-135; trace:e2e p6-073)

A saved CPH number shows on the consignment addresses page as '12/345/6789', with a 'Change' link to the CPH page (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-004; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p12-138; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-045; trace:e2e p6-075, p6-076)
The review page shows the saved CPH number as '12/345/6789', with a 'Change' link to the CPH page (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-120; prototype:dr2-1-specs p4-037)
'Save and continue' on the consignment addresses page goes to the contact address page, for a consignment with a CPH number and for one without (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-121, p12-144)
Reopening the CPH page after saving '12/345/6789' shows 12, 345 and 6789 in its three boxes (repo:frontend p10-038, p10-039)
notes: Combines the addresses page's CPH section (req-700, req-701) with its onward step (req-722, c-116): the same page and the same review.
c-112: the stored value stays nine bare digits; only the display is slashed. The last criterion guards that the round trip still holds.
Shares the addresses page template and the journey flow with the consignment-parties area, and the review page with review-and-submit.

increments.title: With JavaScript, the CPH boxes keep out non-digits and one paste fills all three
increments.detail: Traders often copy the whole CPH number from an APHA document. With JavaScript, each box drops anything that is not a digit as it is typed and stops at its length, and pasting a whole number, with or without slashes, spreads its digits across that box and the ones after it. Without JavaScript the page works as today, with the server's checks as the backstop. Focus is not moved automatically as a box fills (c-006).
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript, typing a letter, space or slash into a CPH box leaves it out, and County, Parish and Holding stop taking digits at 2, 3 and 4 (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-011, p9-012)
With JavaScript, pasting '123456789' or '12/345/6789' into County fills County with 12, Parish with 345 and Holding with 6789 (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-012-m3)
With JavaScript, pasting '3456789' into Parish fills Parish with 345 and Holding with 6789, leaving County as it was (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-012-m3)
Filling a box does not move focus to the next box (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-012)
Without JavaScript, '12/345/6789' pasted into County stays there and saving it shows today's errors, starting with 'County must be 2 digits' (repo:frontend p10-033)
notes: Kept apart from the CPH page row: it is the first client script on this page, needs its own bundle entry and its own with- and without-JavaScript proof, and would push that row past one sitting.
c-006: build the digit filtering and paste spreading, not the automatic focus moves the prototype script makes.
Depends on the CPH page row only in that both change the CPH page; no ordering need, so dependsOn is left empty.

increments.title: The contact address page follows Design Release 2.1: intro, 'Select an address', required choice, no edit card, and on to review
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1's contact page says whose address this is, puts the choice under its own 'Select an address' heading, shows each address without its country, requires a choice before moving on, and goes from there to the review page, its back link returning to the consignment addresses page. It drops today's 'Current contact address' card and the 'Edit details' route: the notification still stores the chosen contact as a copy of its address-book record, shown on the review page, but that copy can no longer be edited apart from its record.
acceptanceCriteria: Directly under the contact page's heading, body text reads 'This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.'; the hint 'Selecting a contact copies their name and address into this notification.' is gone (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-117; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-067, p12-140, p13-123; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-095; trace:e2e p7-006)

Below the intro the page has the sub-heading 'Select an address', and the radios' legend 'Select an address' is visually hidden, so the page heading is no longer the radios' legend (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-118; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-068; repo:frontend p10-058)

Each address option is labelled with the address's name and hinted with its address lines joined by commas, without the country, such as '15 Union Street, Aberdeen, AB11 5BN' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-122; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-070, p13-125; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-098; trace:e2e p7-010, p7-011)

The page shows the address options alone, the current contact pre-selected, with no 'Current contact address' card and no 'Edit details' link, and the contact edit page no longer opens (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-122; trace:e2e p7-026, p8-077)

'Save and continue' with no address chosen shows 'Select a contact address' in the error summary and on the radios, linked to the first option, and saves nothing (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-126; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-075; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-100)

Choosing an address and pressing 'Save and continue' saves it and opens the review page, 'Review your notification', whose contact row shows the chosen address (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-128; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-076, p12-144, p13-126; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-101)

The contact page's back link goes to the consignment addresses page, or to the review page when the page was opened from review (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-132; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-074, p12-143, p13-122; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-112)
A notification with no contact address cannot be submitted (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-135; repo:frontend p10-055)

With the Welsh language chosen, the new intro, 'Select an address' heading and error message show in Welsh, marked as a machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off (repo:frontend p10-083, p10-084)
notes: Combines the contact page's copy and structure (req-753, req-754, req-761), required choice (req-764), navigation (req-766, req-767), submission rule (req-772) and the removal of the current-contact card and edit route (req-774, req-775): one page, one review.

Conflicts followed: c-120 (built now despite DR1's address-space hold), c-122 (a choice is required), c-123 (on to review; back to addresses), c-125 (no card, no edit route; the stored copy stays). The tests repo's contact-page and address-book edit specs change to match.
The add-a-branch link and branch-only list are the next row, which waits on the address book's typed records.

increments.title: The contact address page offers only the trader's own branch addresses and adds a new branch through the address book
increments.detail: The contact is the trader's own branch responsible for the consignment in Great Britain, so the page lists only the organisation's branch addresses, not overseas consignors and other parties. When the right branch is missing, the page tells the trader how to add one: the link opens the address book ready to add a branch address, and on saving the address book returns the trader to the contact page with the new branch chosen and a success banner.
acceptanceCriteria: The contact page offers only the signed-in organisation's own branch addresses, newest added first; consignors, places of origin, consignees, importers, places of destination and transporters in the same address book are not offered (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-123; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p12-141, p13-125; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-097; document:dr1-parity-backlog p6-039 to p6-045; document:dr1-parity-notes p1-019 to p1-023)

On the full stack, under 'Select an address' the page says 'If the correct address is not shown, add a new branch address, then return to this page.', with 'add a new branch address' as the link, and the 'Add a new address' link above the heading is gone; in stub mode, with no address book service, the page offers no way to add an address, as today (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-118; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-069, p12-141, p13-124; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-096; trace:e2e p7-031; repo:tests p1-155)

On the full stack, the link opens the address book's add-address page set to add a 'Branch' address (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-119, p8-120; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-079, p7-082; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-102; trace:e2e p7-032, p7-080)

On the full stack, saving the new branch address returns the trader to the contact page, where the new address is in the list and selected, and the success banner '<name> address added to your address book' shows once and is gone on reload (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-121; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-083, p7-084)

With the Welsh language chosen, the add-a-branch sentence and the success banner show in Welsh, marked as a machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off (repo:frontend p10-084)
notes: Combines the branch-only list (req-760) with the add-a-branch path (req-755, req-756, req-757): both rest on address-book records carrying a type, and on the same round trip through the address book.

c-121: built once the address book's typed record lands, not blocked. Depends on the address-book-add-and-edit area's rows for the 'Branch' type and the record's uses (req-1199, req-1207, req-1253, req-1256); the combiner wires that dependsOn. c-120: the sentence and add path are built now.
Decision: in stub mode (no INS address book, the fit environment) the page keeps today's behaviour of offering no add link, so the add-a-branch criteria are written for the full stack only.
The INS front door's add page must accept the branch type from the handshake; the return already runs through the journey's address-return step by fulfilment id.

increments.title: Which sections the roles and addresses page shows, when its task is complete, and where it continues
increments.detail: Makes the roles and addresses page ask for exactly what the consignment needs and say honestly when it is done. The CPH number is left out for two more germinal product codes; a 'Permanent address' section appears for 01061900 consignments with a species that needs one; the task counts as complete only when every shown section is; and 'Save and continue' goes on to the contact address for this consignment page, or to the overview once everything is complete.
acceptanceCriteria: A consignment whose commodity codes are only 05111000, 05119985, 0101 or 01061900 shows no CPH number row; any other consignment shows it (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-011 to prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-015; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-018, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-025, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-026, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-036)

For commodity code 01061900 with at least one selected species that needs a permanent address, the page shows a 'Permanent address' section with the hint 'A permanent address is where an animal:', the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-013, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-016, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-030; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-019, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-022 to prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-024)
No other consignment shows the 'Permanent address' section (prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-019; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p14-026)

The overview's 'Roles and addresses' task shows Complete only once every party has an address and, where shown, the CPH number or permanent address is given; with any shown section empty it is not Complete (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-039, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-040; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-080)

Uploaded documents', titled 'Document <n>', whose header Change link opens the upload documents page and, on saving, returns to the review (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-104, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-105; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-150, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-156)

Kept as its own row because it owns only the documents card and builds in parallel with the other card rows. The tests repo asserts today's empty-state sentence and follows the new card.

increments.title: Addresses card: permanent addresses, CPH format, one header link and a single unfinished entry
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 shows pets' permanent addresses in full in the Addresses card, writes the CPH with slashes, gives the Addresses and Contact address cards one header Change link and no row actions (c-138), returns a CPH change made from the review to the review (c-141, settling DR1 parity row inc-146's open question), and lists one error summary entry per unfinished card, so a deleted saved address is named once, on its card (c-135).
acceptanceCriteria: Pets' permanent addresses read back in the Addresses card as a 'Permanent address' subsection, one entry per animal labelled '<common name> <n>' (for example 'Domestic cat 1') with the full address and 'United Kingdom', without email or phone, and the identification table has no Permanent address column (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-111; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-152, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-153)
The CPH number reads back with its parts separated by slashes, for example '12/345/6789' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-160, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-154)

No party row and no contact address row carries an 'Edit details' link: the Addresses and Contact address cards' header Change links are their only links (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-067; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-151; c-138)

When the consignor's saved address has been deleted, the error summary holds the single entry 'Complete roles and addresses' linking to the Addresses card, and 'Select an address for the consignor' shows on the consignor's row inside the card, with no separate consignor entry in the summary; the full error list for this case is pinned by a test (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-043; c-135)
notes: Depends on the row 'Review sections and cards take Design Release 2.1's headings, titles and unfinished-card messages' (the Addresses and Contact address cards). Pass 2 combines the Addresses card's read-back slices (permanent addresses, CPH) with its link and error-summary slices (row actions, CPH return, deleted address): all change the same card and its errors. Moving the permanent address out of the identification table touches that table too; the identification row owns the table's other columns. The CPH page's own return behaviour may need the change context the CPH page reads (cph-permanent-and-contact area's page). The tests repo's page object clicks 'Edit details' today and follows the header link.

increments.title: The review page reads each party's copied address back as name, address lines and country
increments.detail: The trader checks the address copy the notification holds before submitting. Design Release 2.1 reads each consignment party and the contact address back as the name followed by the address lines and the country, each on its own line, with no telephone number or email address. Today the review shows each copy as a block with the name in bold and every non-empty field, telephone and email included. Observable in the animals frontend's fit suite, on the compose stack and in CDP.
acceptanceCriteria: On the review page each consignment party with an address reads back as its name, then each non-empty address line, town or city and postcode, then the country, each on its own line (prototype:dr2-1-source p11-065, p11-114; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p12-160, p12-161, p13-151, p13-155)

No party's telephone number or email address appears in the review page's read-back (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p12-160, p13-151; repo:tests p5-040, p5-041)

The contact address for the consignment reads back the same way: name, address lines, country, with no telephone number or email address (prototype:dr2-1-source p11-114; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-151; trace:e2e p8-018)
notes: One requirement on the review page, drafted here because the reconciler gave it to this area. The review page and its party rows are the review-and-submit area's code: combiner, merge this row with that area's review-card row if one changes the same 'Roles and addresses' or contact cards. The end-to-end specs that read every copied field back from the review page (addresses-copied, addresses-submit-freeze, addresses-edit) will need their review assertions updated to the new read-back.

increments.title: Review ends with Continue and Delete, and an amendment's review offers Cancel amend and tells the trader they are re-submitting
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 ends an editable review with Continue and a red Delete. While amending, it adds a 'Cancel amend' button, retitles the review 'Review before re-submitting' once something has changed, and opens with no errors shown. The ruling's validation override still refuses an incomplete resubmission and says why (c-136). What the delete and cancel-amend confirmations do is the manage-notifications area's.
acceptanceCriteria: An editable journey or draft review ends with 'Continue' and, beside it, a red 'Delete' button that opens the notification's delete confirmation (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-115, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-118; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-162, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-157; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-084)

The backend already keeps a pre-amend snapshot of the notification separately from its documents; telling the frontend whether the notification answers differ from it is the backend part of this slice. The tests repo asserts today that a draft review has no Delete, and the cancel-amend spec uses the 'Cancel amendment' link; both follow. Delete and cancel-amend confirmations belong to manage-notifications; this row only links to them.

increments.title: A notification opened from the dashboard has a view header: reference, status, dates and a Back link to the overall dashboard
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 heads a notification opened from the dashboard with its reference and status, dates it, and sends the trader back to the overall dashboard, which is the INS front door's (c-143, c-198). A draft opened this way stays editable and lists what is incomplete. The page title keeps the page name before the service, as accessibility requires (c-006). An unknown reference goes to the dashboard.

Status tags for 'Submitted action required' and 'Submission complete'/'Completed' are the action-required and completed rows'. 'Copy as new', 'Delete' and 'Amend this notification' in the header are the header-actions row's.

increments.title: View header offers Amend, Copy as new and Delete, and shows the import reference numbers to copy
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 offers 'Amend this notification' on a submitted notification, 'Copy as new' and 'Delete' on every viewed notification, drafts included, and gives the trader the notification reference and customs document code they need for the customs declaration, each with a Copy button. Each state-changing control looks as Design Release 2.1 draws it but submits a form with the CSRF token (c-189). What amend, copy and delete do is the manage-notifications area's.

increments.title: Submitting records its date and outstanding items, and a notification still missing its health certificate shows as 'Submitted action required'
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 records the submission date and what is still outstanding at the declaration, and shows a notification submitted without its health certificate as 'Submitted action required': read-only, with a warning saying what to do, the missing certificate marked in section 4, and a Continue that leads back to the hub. The real service can only change a submitted notification through an amendment, so that Continue starts one (c-144). Identifier-driven items wait on DR1 inc-103 (c-133) and are a separate blocked row.

Uploaded documents' shows the error 'Upload a valid health certificate' in place of document cards, inline, with no error summary (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-107; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-099)

The backend stores the outstanding items worked out at submission (today the confirmation page works out its documents item on the fly, and the declaration saves only the tick); a re-submission from an amendment records them afresh. Uses the same ITAHC-or-health-certificate test as the confirmation page row (req-929). req-904's fallback warning is in this draft's unobservable list. The dashboard flag for the same state is the 'Action required on the dashboard' row.

increments.title: Notification submitted page follows Design Release 2.1's guard, wording and links
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 guards the submitted (confirmation) page on the declaration, asks for the ITAHC by name and checks for one rather than for any document, tells the trader they can view or change the notification from the dashboard, sends 'Return to your dashboard' to the overall dashboard in the INS front door (c-143), makes 'Create a new notification' a link to the create notification start page, and opens the HMRC links in a new tab.

increments.title: A completed notification shows as complete with no Amend button
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 shows a finished notification as 'Submission complete' (or its own status text, such as 'Completed') and stops amendment. increments.title: Tests prove the review, declaration and confirmation paths no test covers today
increments.detail: Today's suites leave several review, declaration and confirmation paths unproven, and many of them change in this programme. After this row each one has a test that fails if the behaviour breaks.
acceptanceCriteria: A test proves the review of a notification with several commodity lines reads back each commodity card and each species block with its rows (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p13-133; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p25-087)

A test proves the review's party address errors: a copied address that breaks the address-book rules and a deleted saved address each show their messages and links (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p13-134; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p13-071)

A test proves how the review shows a rejected document and a document still being scanned (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p13-134; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p25-088; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p13-067)

A test proves Cancel amend on the amendment review and each view header button (Amend this notification, Copy as new, Delete) leads where it should (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p13-133; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p13-101, trace-e2e-p13-105)

A test proves the confirmation page for a notification submitted with an ITAHC uploaded shows no outstanding documents item (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p14-063; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p26-057)

A test proves the declaration's refusal path: a ticked declaration on a notification the review refuses is not submitted and the trader is told why (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p14-064; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p26-059)

A test proves a failed submit and a stale submit (a notification changed or already submitted elsewhere) leave the notification unsubmitted and tell the trader (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p14-064; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p26-060)

A test proves a declaration ticked on an incomplete notification is refused and the trader is sent back to the review naming what is missing (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p14-064; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p14-021; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-087)
notes: Depends on every todo row in this area whose behaviour it proves (commodity cards, Addresses card, documents cards, amendment review, view header actions, confirmation page), so each test asserts the Design Release 2.1 behaviour rather than today's. Each criterion is proved at whichever level fits (frontend fit spec or the tests repo's end-to-end suite); the planner picks. A failed or stale submit is driven through the backend's real refusal, mocked only at the network boundary in fit tests.

increments.title: Overview totals count only positive numbers
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1's Overview adds only positive counts to the Animals and Packages/boxes totals, so a card never shows a negative or odd total. Held until the reconciler says how such a count could reach the Overview.
acceptanceCriteria: On the Overview, the Animals and Packages/boxes totals add only the positive counts on each commodity line: a zero, negative or non-numeric count adds nothing, and a total that is not above zero reads '0' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-014, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-015; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p4-010)
openQuestions: Sent back to the reconciler: no trader can enter a zero, negative or non-numeric count (the commodity details page refuses any number of animals or packages below 1, and a template is seeded from the same checked answers), so the change cannot be observed in any environment. The reconciler decides whether req-787 is already met as far as anyone can observe, or names how such a count can reach the Overview.
notes: Drafted by the combiner: the notification-hub drafter listed req-787 as unobservable. It is held here, blocked on the reconciler's answer, so the buildable Overview rows are not held up.

Dropped: the reconciler adopted req-787 as already met (delta exists). Commodity details refuses a number of animals or packages below 1 or not whole, and templates are seeded from the same checked answers, so no zero, negative or non-numeric count can reach the Overview; blank counts already add nothing and both totals already read 0 before any line exists.

increments.title: Fallback warning for an action-required notification's other outstanding items

The reconciler names an outstanding item that triggers it, or puts req-904 out of scope until one exists.

Dropped: the reconciler put req-904 out of scope. increments.title: Amend this notification asks for confirmation in a dialog, then opens the amend review
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks a trader to confirm before amending a submitted notification, in a dialog over the view page, and then takes them straight to the notification's review page so they can see and change their answers. Today the amend action has no confirmation and lands on the overview hub, one step away from the review. After this change 'Amend this notification' opens a modal dialog ('Amend notification', 'Are you sure you want to change this notification?') whose 'Yes, continue' starts the amendment and lands on the amend review, the dashboard card's Amend lands on the same review, and an amend that cannot happen returns the trader to the overall dashboard. Because a state change must stay a form post carrying the CSRF token (c-189), the dialog's confirm submits a form, and without script the same control reaches a confirmation page with the dialog's heading, question and buttons (c-190).
acceptanceCriteria: On a Submitted notification's view page, 'Amend this notification' opens, without leaving the page, a dialog with the level-1 heading 'Amend notification' and the question 'Are you sure you want to change this notification?' increments.title: Copy as new carries over exactly Design Release 2.1's list, from the submitted version
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 says what a copy keeps (origin, internal reference, what is imported with its species, the reasons and their follow-ups, the additional animal details, the parties and CPH) and what it leaves for the trader to fill in again (numbers of animals and packages, identifiers, arrival, transit, transporter, documents and contact address). Today the backend copy mapper and the pages disagree: the record clears the internal reference, the species, the unweaned answer and the exit date, yet the copy's overview shows counts, identification, arrival, transit, transport and contact address as Complete because the whole answer payload is copied. c-196 settles that a copy carries exactly Design Release 2.1's list, in the record and on the pages alike, and c-197 that copying an amendment in progress copies its submitted version. After this change a copy keeps and clears what Design Release 2.1 says, and a certified-for value no longer offered is mapped to a current one.
acceptanceCriteria: A copy's origin of the import comes back with the source's internal reference number, and the copy's review shows it (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-063; c-196)

increments.title: A stale Copy as new from the view page returns to the view page with the updated banner
increments.detail: Copy as new is checked against the version of the notification the trader was looking at, so a copy of something that has changed since is refused with 'The notification has been updated'. increments.title: After a delete the trader lands on the overall dashboard, and the notification list then says '<reference> has been deleted'; an amending notification can be deleted

increments.title: The live animals list moves to the INS frontend, scoped to the trader's organisation
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 serves the category notification lists in the same service as the overall home. Following Rhys's DR1 judgement that the animals dashboard is temporary and moves to the INS front door (c-159), the INS frontend serves the live animals list at /live-animals from the INS backend read model, and the animals frontend's own dashboard at its set root sends the trader there. The page takes Design Release 2.1's frame: the 'Dashboard' title and caption, the 'Live animals' heading, a Back link to the home, 'Create new' and 'Use template' buttons in place of today's start form, the 'Notifications' heading, and cards labelled for screen readers. Persistence and authentication are real constraints, so the list shows only the signed-in trader's organisation's notifications and the list API refuses a caller that names no organisation. Every new string ships with a Welsh machine draft. This row sets the page, the cross-service hop and the scoping every later list row builds on.

The search matches a notification's number, commodity, consignee or consignor, which needs the INS read model to hold the consignee and consignor; the sort is always applied, newest first by default, with no unsorted state (DR1 judgement).
