Searching for part of a listed notification's number, its commodity, its consignee's name or its consignor's name lists only the notifications that match; a search with surrounding spaces finds the same notifications, and a blank search lists them all (conflicts:c-dashboard-home-012; repo:insfrontend src/server/app/features/dashboard/controller.js:89-90; repo:tests domain/ins/models/db/aggregated-notification-document.ts:1-10)
A search that matches nothing shows 'Show 0 of 0 results' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:7644-7658)

The 'Sort by:' select offers 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', with 'Newest first' selected by default and no 'Select one' option; choosing each re-orders the list accordingly (trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed snapshot 14; document:dr1-parity-notes inc-031; conflicts:c-dashboard-home-014)

Searching from page 2 keeps the page as a hidden field, and page links keep the chosen sort and category (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-actions.html:43-87; trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed action 25)
notes: Kept apart from the Action needed page row so that row stays reviewable and because this one changes what the read model stores (consignee and consignor, from the trade parties already in the animals backend's published notification) and how it searches. The same search form, sort select and results line are reused by the blocked Inspection required drill-down, which proves its own half of req-dashboard-home-040 and -042. Depends on the Action needed page row.

increments.title: Glance cards on the home's category sections
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 summarises each category on the home with glance cards. The Live animals section gets its Action needed card, counted from the same set its drill-down lists for the signed-in organisation (the prototype's fixed numbers are overruled). The plants section gets its three cards, linked as the live-animals ones are (open question default); their counts wait until plants notifications reach the INS read model, so they show no number yet. The live-animals Status updates card waits with its blocked drill-down. Cards carry DR2.1's styling.
acceptanceCriteria: The Live animals section shows an 'Action needed' glance card reading 'Tasks requiring your attention', with a count and a 'View tasks' link to /actions?category=live-animals (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:57-62; trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 34; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:43)

The Action needed count equals the number of results /actions?category=live-animals lists for the signed-in organisation: it is 0 for a fresh organisation, and goes up by one when that organisation submits a live-animals notification without its ITAHC (conflicts:c-dashboard-home-004; conflicts:c-dashboard-home-005)
The Live animals section shows no Inspection required card (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:125-130; trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 30)

The Action needed card's count uses the default count colour, matching the prototype's glance cards (trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 30 .app-dr2-dashboard-glance-card; conflicts:c-dashboard-home-013)

The home with its glance cards still has no serious or critical axe violations against the WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA tags, and its card copy is shown in Welsh with Welsh selected (repo:insfrontend src/server/app/features/dashboard/dashboard.fit.spec.js:8-20; copy.cy.js)
openQuestions: What makes a notification 'Action needed'? Default followed: a submitted notification still missing a required document; the count is the size of that list (conflicts:c-dashboard-home-005).
notes: Combines every glance card that can be built now: they share the home template and the card styling. Depends on the home row (sections) and the Action needed page row (the count is that list's total). The plants 'View updates' and 'View requirements' links point at the Status updated and Inspection required drill-downs, which are blocked; until they land those two links lead to a not-found page, as the default accepts. The live-animals Status updates card (req-dashboard-home-024) is held with its blocked drill-down, following c-dashboard-home-004: a card whose state no service records waits rather than shipping an always-zero count.

Combiner: req-982 (the plants section's three glance cards) is blocked until the plants services publish to the INS read model, so it and its criteria moved to the blocked row 'The plants section's glance cards'; this row builds the live-animals cards only.

increments.title: The list has 'In progress', 'Draft' and 'Completed' tabs
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 splits the list into three tabs, each a link that loads the page. 'In progress' holds submitted, action-required and amending notifications and shows its count; 'Draft' holds drafts; 'Completed' holds completed ones. Each tab's cards sit under an h3 naming it. The list API gains the category and tab filters and the In progress count.
acceptanceCriteria: The list has three tabs, 'In progress', 'Draft' and 'Completed', each a link that loads the page: 'In progress' the list path, 'Draft' ?tab=drafts and 'Completed' ?tab=completed; a missing or unknown tab shows 'In progress'. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-037, prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-038; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-061; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-042, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-054)
A tab link carries no search, sort or filter, so following a tab drops them. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-038-m1; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-056)

'In progress' lists the organisation's submitted and action-required notifications and its notifications being amended, each amending one with its yellow 'Amending' tag and Resume, 'Copy as new', 'Cancel amendment' and Delete; it lists no draft. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-039; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-073; conflict c-165)

'Draft' lists only drafts, and 'Completed' lists no draft, submitted or amending notification. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-039; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-075)

Only 'In progress' shows a count, in bold brackets, such as 'In progress (2)', counting the notifications that tab lists; 'Draft' and 'Completed' show no count, even when selected. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-037; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-062; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-043)

Under the tabs the cards sit under an h3 naming the tab: 'Notifications in progress', 'Draft notifications' or 'Completed notifications'. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-040; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-063; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-044, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-055, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-057)

The list API filters by category and by tab (the in-progress statuses, drafts, or completed) and reports how many notifications the 'In progress' tab holds for that category. (repo:insbackend repo-insbackend-p1-021, repo-insbackend-p1-044, repo-insbackend-p1-045)

The category filter lands here, with the tab filter, because the category is first in the read model from the card-facts row; req-1093 (each list only its category) is proven with the germinal products list. Completed notifications cannot exist until the authorities' outcome feed (req-1082, blocked row), so the Completed tab is proven empty of everything else.

increments.title: Search and sort become one form that really searches and sorts
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 puts search, sort and the additional filters in one column above the tabs, submitted by one icon-only search button, with a 'Search by' field whose hint names what it searches. Because the real service can query stored notifications (c-162), the search really matches any part of the reference, commodity, consignee or consignor, ignoring case, and the three sorts really order the list. Following DR1's judgement on inc-031 (c-161), the list is always sorted and has no 'Select one' option. The separate sort form and its 'Update sort' button go.
acceptanceCriteria: The search and sort sit in one column above the tabs inside the 'Notifications' section; there is no 'Filter notifications' heading and no filter column beside the results. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-045; conflict c-167)

The search field is labelled 'Search by' and has the hint 'Keyword, notification number, commodity, consignee or consignor'. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-027; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-046; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-039, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-040)

The search is submitted by an icon-only button showing a magnifying glass, announced to screen readers as 'Search', and submits to the server, so a trader without JavaScript searches the same way. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-027; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-047; conflict c-006)

Searching any part of a notification's reference number, commodity, consignee or consignor, in any case and with spaces around it, lists every notification of the organisation that contains it, paged like any other list; searching text none contains lists none. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-027; ruling:sam-2026-10-07 ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-010; repo:insbackend repo-insbackend-p1-059; conflict c-162)

Search, sort and the other list controls are one GET form to the list's own path, submitted by the search button, carrying the current tab (unless 'In progress') and the current page (when above 1), so the result stays on that tab. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-026, prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-036; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-049, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-050; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-058)

The sort select is labelled 'Sort by:' and offers exactly 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', in that order, with no 'Select one' option. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-028; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p3-045; conflict c-161)

'Newest first' and 'Oldest first' order the cards by when each notification was created, 'Arrival date' by arrival date newest first, and with no sort chosen the cards are in arrival date order, newest first, with 'Arrival date' selected. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-028; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-053; document:dr1-parity-notes document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-012; conflict c-161, c-162)

Paging through a sorted list never shows a notification twice or leaves one out, even when several share the same created or arrival date. (repo:insbackend repo-insbackend-p1-046, repo-insbackend-p1-047; repo:backend repo-backend-p3-006)

There is no 'Update sort' button: the search button applies the chosen sort, and the chosen sort stays selected after the page reloads. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-028, prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-036; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-051)

Already met and kept: the field keeps its text and a blank search lists everything (req-1047). The additional filters join this form in the next row. The prototype's inert search and sort (c-162) and its unselected 'Select one' (c-161) are not built.

increments.title: The list has 'Additional filters' for arrival date, date range and status
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 adds a collapsible 'Additional filters' section to the list's form: arrival-date radios, a date range with two MOJ date pickers, and a status select. The real service applies each filter (c-162) and, because validation is a real constraint (c-166), tells the trader when a date cannot be read or the range ends before it starts.
acceptanceCriteria: The list has a collapsible 'Additional filters' section with a chevron, closed when the page loads with no filter set and open whenever an arrival-date, date-range or status filter is set. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-030; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-054; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-049)

A 'By arrival date' column offers small radios 'Today', 'Tomorrow' and 'Next 7 days' (the legend visually hidden, the same words shown as its heading); choosing one lists only notifications arriving in that range, and the choice stays checked. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-031; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-055, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-060; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-050; conflict c-162)

A 'By date range' column has the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026' and two MOJ date pickers, 'Start date' and 'End date', each with a 'Choose date' calendar opening on the current month with weeks starting on Monday; the list shows only notifications arriving between the two dates, and the entered dates are kept. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-056, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-057, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-121; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-051, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-052; conflict c-162)
A start date alone lists notifications arriving on or after it, and an end date alone those arriving on or before it. (repo:insbackend repo-insbackend-p1-044, repo-insbackend-p1-045; conflict c-162)

When the start date cannot be read as a date the list shows a GOV.UK error summary and an inline error 'Enter a real start date'; for the end date 'Enter a real end date'; when the end date is before the start date 'End date must be the same as or after the start date'. In each case 'Additional filters' is open, the entered text stays in the pickers, and the list is shown without the date-range filter. (ruling:sam-2026-10-07 ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-010; conflict c-166)

A 'Status' select offers exactly 'Select one', 'Action required', 'Submitted' and 'Completed'; choosing a status lists only notifications in it, and the choice stays selected. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-035; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-058; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-053; conflict c-162)
The filters apply together with the search, the sort and the current tab, all submitted by the search button. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-036; conflict c-162)
notes: Combines the collapsible section, the three filter columns, the date validation and the API filters: one section of one form over one query. The INS frontend has no MOJ frontend package today (the animals frontend has @ministryofjustice/frontend 11.1.0); adding it, and its build entries, is part of this row and a shared build-config change. The 'Action required' status option lists what the dashboard-home area's action-needed derivation marks (req-988), and 'Completed' lists nothing until the authorities' outcome feed exists (req-1082, blocked row); both options render and filter now. The prototype's lack of date validation is overruled (c-166).

increments.title: The list pages 8 at a time with numbered pages and no results line or empty messages
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 shows 8 notifications a page with GOV.UK numbered pagination, no results count, and an empty list with no message when nothing matches or a tab is empty. Page links keep everything that shaped the list, because the real search and filters apply (c-163). A page number out of range lands on the nearest real page.
acceptanceCriteria: The list shows 8 notifications a page. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-041)

A list of more than one page shows GOV.UK pagination with numbered page links, a 'Previous' link from page 2 and a 'Next' link on every page before the last; a list of one page, or with no results, shows no pagination. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-042)
A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and a page past the last shows the last page. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-041; repo:insbackend repo-insbackend-p1-029)

Page links keep the tab (unless 'In progress'), the sort (unless the default), the search text and every additional filter. (ruling:sam-2026-10-07 ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-010; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p3-034; conflict c-163)

The list shows no results count: no 'Showing 1 Result', 'Showing S to E of T Results', 'Showing N of T Results' or 'No Results' line. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-044; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-077; conflict c-167)
A search or filter that matches nothing shows an empty list with no message; 'No notifications found' is gone. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-045)

increments.title: The list's Summary shows 'Action needed' and 'Status updated' glance cards

The count depends on the action-needed derivation the dashboard-home area builds in the animals backend and the INS read model (req-988, c-149); the combiner should make this row depend on that row and reuse the home's glance-card component rather than build a second one. increments.title: The list's success banner is titled 'Success' and shown once
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 shows a success notification banner titled 'Success' carrying the action's message when an action returns the trader to the list. Today the banner is titled for the action and shows whenever the address carries ?deleted=1 or ?copied=1. The message is held for the trader and shown once instead. The banner still stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page (c-006).
acceptanceCriteria: After deleting a notification from its card, the trader is back on the live animals list, which shows a GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert, titled 'Success', carrying the message 'The notification has been deleted.' (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p3-062, repo-frontend-p3-064; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-115)
Reloading the list, or opening it again, after the banner has shown does not show it again. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-114)
Opening the list with ?deleted=1 or ?copied=1 in its address shows no banner. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p3-062, repo-frontend-p3-063)
openQuestions: How a message from an action run in the animals frontend reaches the INS frontend list once, when the two frontends keep separate sessions. Default: the animals frontend hands the INS frontend a single-use message reference on the redirect, which the INS frontend reads once and which shows nothing on any later visit; the plan settles the mechanism and says so.
notes: Combines the banner's title and its show-once behaviour: one banner. Kept as they are (already met): the banner does not dismiss itself (req-1088, c-006), and the stale-action and 'There is a problem' banners (req-1089), which must still show on the INS frontend list after the move. The prototype's 5-second auto-dismiss is overruled (c-006). Which actions return to the list, and the action routes themselves, belong to manage-notifications; the combiner should order this row after that area's delete row if it moves the delete's redirect.

increments.title: Start a template: notification type, template name and origin in template mode
increments.detail: A trader starts a new template from Manage templates. 'Create new template' asks the notification type question, then a template name page, then opens Origin of the import in template mode, where the page carries a 'Template' caption with the template's name. The name is optional and unvalidated. Starting a template never creates or changes a notification. This row sets the template-mode pattern (caption, buttons and back link) every later template-mode question page follows.
acceptanceCriteria: Manage templates has a primary 'Create new template' button, a link styled as a button; following it shows 'What are you importing?' under the caption 'About the consignment', with the radios Live animals, Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos), Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products, none preselected, a 'Continue' button, a Back link to Manage templates and no 'Template' caption; continuing with no choice shows the page's usual error (prototype:dr2-1-source dashboard-templates.html:50-53, app/routes.js:8958-8964; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T9 action 11; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:20, 124-127)

Continuing from the type question goes to the template name page, titled 'Enter template name - Import notification service - GOV.UK', with the caption 'Create a new template', the H1 'Enter template name', one text input labelled by the H1 with the visually hidden label 'Enter template name', and no hint (prototype:dr2-1-source create-template.html:8,30-45; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T9 action 23; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:128-136)

The template name page has a 'Save and continue' button and a 'Cancel and return to manage templates' link to Manage templates (prototype:dr2-1-source create-template.html:48-55; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:137)

The template name page's Back link goes to the type question when a type has been chosen, and to Manage templates otherwise (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8980; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:138)

A blank name moves on to Origin of the import with no error, and no length, character or duplicate-name rule is applied; spaces around a name are trimmed (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8984-9002; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T10 actions 11-13; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:174-179)
Going back to the name page part way through creating a template shows the name already entered; starting a new template shows it empty (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8966-8975)

While a new template is being created, Origin of the import shows a 'Template' caption with the template name above the caption 'About the consignment', asks the same questions with the same hints and guidance as for a notification (country search, region of origin, internal reference), offers only 'Save and continue' with no Cancel link, and its Back link returns to the template name page (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T11 action 14, T9 actions 30-38; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:146-147)

Starting and naming a template creates no notification and changes none: the user's notifications on the dashboard are the same before and after, and the chosen notification type is kept on the template in progress (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8989-9001; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:140-142)

notes: Combines the start of template creation: the button (req-templates-003), the type question in template mode (-023, -024, -025), the name page (-026 to -028, -030 to -033) and the first template-mode question page (-034, -035). They are one journey a reviewer walks once; split, none can be seen alone. Depends on the Manage templates row, and on the start-and-origin row that builds the type question. Backend is listed so the plan can hold the template in progress in the template store rather than as a notification; if the plan holds it elsewhere, the backend repo carries no change in this row. increments.detail: While a template is being created, 'What are you importing?' returns to the template's own task list, which is headed 'Template tasklist', shows a 'Template' tag and the template name, has five sections with no Documents section, and ends with 'Review template' and 'Return to manage templates'. In template mode, opening Upload documents returns to the template's task list, and opening the declaration goes to the template review (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T9 actions 57-60; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:153-157)

increments.title: Save a template and see it on Manage templates
increments.detail: 'Save template' stores the template, even part answered, and returns to Manage templates with a success banner and the new template first in the list. Each card shows its title and links to view or use it. Templates are kept by the backend between sessions and belong to the user who saved them. A template saved with no name is 'Untitled template'.
acceptanceCriteria: The template review has a 'Save template' button that posts the form; saving, even with only some sections answered, returns to Manage templates with the new template first in the list and the count one higher, such as 'Show 1-1 of 1 results' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T9 actions 72-78; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:166-169; conflicts:c-templates-006)

After saving, Manage templates shows a GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert, titled 'Success', headed '<template title> saved to templates'; it shows once, not again on reload, and with JavaScript on it dismisses itself after 5 seconds (prototype:dr2-1-source dashboard-templates.html:24-37, app/routes.js:8932-8936, 9010; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T5 action 26)

A template saved with no name is titled 'Untitled template': the banner reads 'Untitled template saved to templates' and it is listed first (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T10 actions 14-16; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:174, 182)

Each template is a card labelled 'Template <title>' showing the template's category label above its title, which is an H3, with a 'View template' link to the template's page and a 'Use template' link (prototype:dr2-1-source partials/design-release-2.1/dashboard-template-card.html:2-11; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 actions 19-24; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:24-25)
The list shows the user's saved templates newest saved first (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:7680-7689, 7808-7818)

A new template's address is built from its title in lower case with every run of other characters replaced by a hyphen ('template' if nothing is left), with -2, -3 and on added when the user already has a template with that address: two templates both named 'Weekly cattle' get distinct addresses (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:7695-7712)
A saved template is still listed after the user signs out and signs back in (ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claim 6; conflicts:c-templates-001)

(conflicts:c-templates-002)

increments.title: Use a template to start a notification

A template's category label reads 'Germinal products' when its notification holds only germinal products, and 'Live animals' otherwise (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:7752)

A template saves the place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and contact address each as answered, and its page's Addresses and Contact address cards show each of them (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T3 action 20; conflicts:c-templates-004 default)

Where the contact address was not chosen, the template uses the place of origin as its contact address, as the design does (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:7800-7802; conflicts:c-templates-004 default)

A notification started from a template has each party and the contact address seeded as the template holds them (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:7968-7985, 8069-8086, 8108-8120; conflicts:c-templates-004 default)

sources.ref: T3 action 20; T9 action 78; T10 action 16

openQuestions: Should a template save and reuse each party's address separately (consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination), or, as Design Release 2.1 does, save the place of origin and use it for every party? Default followed: save each party's address and the contact address separately as answered, show them on the template page and as the card's Consignee and Consignor, and seed each back into a notification started from it; where the contact address was not chosen, use the place of origin. (conflicts:c-templates-004)
notes: Kept apart because it carries the party-address question the other rows do not. Combines the card's answer rows (req-templates-014), the category rule (-015) and party addresses (-056): the card's Consignee and Consignor come from the same saved party addresses. Depends on the save row (cards), the view row (template page cards) and the use row (seeding), since its criteria are seen on all three. Germinal products can only be chosen once the commodities area's germinal products row lands; the category criterion's germinal half waits on it, the combiner should add that dependency.

increments.title: Sort the templates list
increments.detail: Manage templates has a 'Sort by:' select. Following the default for the sort question, it works the same way as the dashboard's sort, including without JavaScript: Newest first and Oldest first order by date created, and 'Select one' and 'Arrival date' keep the newest-first order.
acceptanceCriteria: Manage templates has a 'Sort by:' select with the options 'Select one', 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', preselecting the option that matches the current sort (prototype:dr2-1-source dashboard-templates.html:63-74; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 24)

With two or more templates, choosing 'Oldest first' lists them oldest date created first, and 'Newest first' newest first, with and without JavaScript, the same way the dashboard's sort applies (conflicts:c-templates-003 default)
'Select one' and 'Arrival date' keep the default newest-first order (conflicts:c-templates-003 default)
openQuestions: Should the templates list's Sort by select work, and if so what should 'Arrival date' do for templates that hold no arrival date? Default followed: build the select with the four options as designed, working the same way as the dashboard's sort (including without JavaScript): Newest first and Oldest first order by date created, 'Select one' and 'Arrival date' keep the default newest-first order. (conflicts:c-templates-003)
notes: Kept apart: it carries the sort question no other row does. Depends on the save row (two templates are needed to see an order). How the dashboard's sort submits (the notification-list area's sort row) is the pattern to copy; the combiner should order this row after that one.

increments.title: Edit a whole saved template on its own task list
increments.detail: A saved template can be reopened at its edit address on its own template task list. Saving it from the review overwrites the template, keeping its address, and moves it to the top of the list.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening a saved template's edit address opens the template's task list ('Template tasklist', 'Template' tag and name) with the template's answers filled in (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8551-8569; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:88-90)

Saving the edited template from its review overwrites it: the list count is unchanged, the template keeps its address, shows the changed answer, and is listed first (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:7751, 7808-7818)
The edit address of a template that does not exist goes to Manage templates (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8556-8560)
notes: Combines opening the edit (req-templates-072) and saving over the template (-051): an edit is only seen whole once saved. Depends on the save row.The template page has no Edit link (req-templates-061): the address is reached directly, so tests open it by address. The review's Delete button for a saved template being edited is in the delete row.

increments.title: Discard a template being created
increments.detail: A template being created can be thrown away from its review, through the same 'Delete this template?' confirmation, without being saved. The confirmation uses the journey layout.
acceptanceCriteria: The template review's red warning 'Delete' button, for a template being created, opens a page with the H1 'Delete this template?', a one-row summary list keyed 'Name' holding the name entered ('this template' when none), 'Confirm that you want to delete this template.' and 'This action cannot be undone.', and a Back link and 'No, cancel' link to the template review (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8571-8587; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T11 actions 14-21; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:185-195)
The discard confirmation uses the journey layout, not the dashboard layout (prototype:dr2-1-source delete-template.html:1,23)

Confirming 'Yes, delete' throws the template away unsaved and returns to Manage templates, list and count unchanged, with the success banner '<template name> has been deleted', or 'Template has been deleted' when no name was entered (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8589-8600; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T11 actions 25-28; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:197-199)

Opening the discard page when no template is being created goes to Manage templates, and posting to it then changes nothing and returns to Manage templates (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8572-8574; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T12 actions 7-8; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:202-204)
notes: Combines the discard page (req-templates-090), its guard (-091), the outcome (-092) and the journey layout rule (-088, which the delete row's confirmation also keeps). The prototype's unguarded discard post is not reproduced (req-templates-096 out of scope). Depends on the review row. The 'Delete' button's half for a saved template is req-templates-049, in the delete row.

increments.title: Delete a saved template
increments.detail: A saved template can be deleted from its page, or from its review while it is being edited, through a 'Delete this template?' confirmation. Deleting removes it and returns to Manage templates with a banner.
acceptanceCriteria: The template page's 'Delete' button opens a page titled 'Delete this template? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' with the H1 'Delete this template?', using the journey layout (prototype:dr2-1-source delete-template.html:1,6,23, app/routes.js:8616-8618; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T8 actions 8-11; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:102-107)

The confirmation shows a one-row summary list keyed 'Name' holding the template's title, then 'Confirm that you want to delete this template.' and 'This action cannot be undone.' (prototype:dr2-1-source delete-confirmation.html:6-11; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T8 actions 12-14; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:109-111)

It has a red warning 'Yes, delete' button and a 'No, cancel' link back to the template page in a GOV.UK button group, and a Back link to the template page (prototype:dr2-1-source delete-confirmation.html:13-21; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T8 actions 15-18; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:112)

Confirming 'Yes, delete' removes the template and returns to Manage templates with one template fewer in the count and the success banner '<title> has been deleted'; the template's page then goes to Manage templates (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8627-8657; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T8 actions 22-29; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:114-117)

On the template review, the red warning 'Delete' button goes to the discard confirmation for a template being created, and to the delete confirmation for a saved template being edited (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T9 action 68; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:166)
The delete address of a template that does not exist goes to Manage templates (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8608-8612, 8633-8637)
notes: Combines the delete confirmation (req-templates-083 to -087), the outcome and banner (-089, -019) and the review's Delete button (-049), whose saved-template half needs this page and the edit row. Depends on the view, edit and discard rows. Deleted templates are removed from the store, so the prototype's seeded-template resurrection does not arise (conflict c-templates-001).

increments.title: Commodity pages return to where the trader came from: check answers, the overview or a template
increments.detail: A trader who opens the commodity pages from check answers, the overview or a template's review should come back there, not walk on through the journey. After a change from check answers, a valid Save and continue on both the commodity page and Commodity details returns to check answers, carried by the real service's change context; from the overview it returns to the overview; while editing a template from its review it returns to the template; and while creating a template a valid Save and continue on the commodity page goes to the overview.
acceptanceCriteria: After choosing Change on a commodity answer from check answers, a valid Save and continue on the commodity page and on Commodity details returns to check answers. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-100; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p5-038; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-103)
Opened from the overview, a valid Save and continue on Commodity details returns to the overview. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-100)

While editing a template from its review, a valid Save and continue on the commodity page and on Commodity details returns to the template's review. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-100)
While a trader is creating a template, a valid Save and continue on the commodity page goes to the notification overview. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-100)
notes: Combines the change-context return (req-119) with the template-creation return (req-091): both are where the commodity pages go back to, on the same two controllers. c-021 (ruled): Commodity details returns to check answers too, carried by ?change=1. Depends on the row 'Commodity pages chain as journey steps around the main import reason' in this area, and on the templates area's rows that let a trader create a template and edit it from its review: the real service has no notification templates today, so the template criteria cannot be observed until those land. The combiner sets both dependencies.

increments.title: Main import reason page edits a template from its review
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader edit a template page by page from the template's review. Opened that way, the main import reason page's Back link goes to the template's review, and saving saves the template and returns there with a confirmation.
acceptanceCriteria: Opened from a template's review, the main import reason page's Back link goes to that template's review (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-009)

Opened from a template's review, a valid 'Save and continue' saves the reason to the template and returns to the template's review, showing '<title> has been updated' with the template's title (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-009)
The template's review then shows the reason just saved, and the notification the template came from is unchanged (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-009)
notes: Kept apart because it needs the templates area's rows that let a template be created and edited from its review (req-1327, req-1331, req-1352): the combiner should make it depend on them, or merge it into the templates row that brings editing to each journey page if that row covers every page. No template mode exists in the real frontend today.

increments.title: Arrival details while creating or editing a template
increments.detail: A template is reused across consignments, so a one-off arrival date does not belong in it: while a template is being created, arrival details does not ask for the arrival date and the section is complete without one. A trader editing a template from its review is sent back to the template review.
acceptanceCriteria: While a template is being created, arrival details shows no arrival date question, and the other four questions are shown as usual (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-022; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p11-007)

While a template is being created, saving arrival details saves no arrival date, and the template's arrival details count as complete once the port of entry, means of transport, transport identification and transport document reference are given (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-023, prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-056)

When arrival details is opened to edit a template from its review, the Back link goes to the template review (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-006; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p11-006)

When arrival details is opened to edit a template from its review, Save and continue saves and returns to the template review (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-053, prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-083)
notes: Combines req-290 (no arrival date in a template) and req-291 (return to template review): both are arrival details' behaviour in template mode. The frontend has no templates today, so this row depends on the templates area's rows that create a template through the journey and add the template review page; the combiner must set that dependsOn. If the templates area adds backend fields, they land there, not here. Kept apart from the other arrival rows so they are not held up by templates.

increments.title: Template creation leaves out Upload documents
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 keeps documents out of templates, because a document belongs to one consignment: while a trader is creating a template, Upload documents is not a step of the journey, and opening or submitting the page goes to the overview without saving anything. No real service has templates yet, so this lands once the templates area has built template creation.
acceptanceCriteria: While creating a template, Save and continue on the transporter step goes to Consignment addresses, passing over Upload documents. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1517-1525)
While creating a template, opening the Upload documents page's address goes to the template's overview. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:12185-12187)
While creating a template, submitting the Upload documents page goes to the template's overview and the template holds no document. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:12207-12209)
notes: Kept apart: it can only be observed once template creation exists, which the templates area builds. The combiner must make this row depend on the templates area's row that lets a trader create a template and walk its journey; that is a real ordering need, not a layer split. Where template mode lives in the shared flow is for the templates area's rows to set.

increments.title: The transporter list's buttons when amending a notification or editing a template
increments.detail: When the transporter list is reached while amending a submitted notification, or while editing a template from its review, it ends with the controls DR2.1 gives those modes, so the trader can return to where they came from.
acceptanceCriteria: When the notification is being amended, the transporter list ends with a primary 'Save and return' that goes back to the review, a secondary 'Save and continue' and a link-style 'Save and return to overview'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html isAmend branch)

When the transporter list is edited from a template review, it ends with a single 'Save and return' button, which goes back to the template, and a 'Cancel' link back to the template. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html isTemplateReview branch; app/routes.js:3335)
notes: Combines the two alternative-mode control sets (req-029, -030): both change only the list's closing controls. Needs amending a notification (the manage-notifications area) and editing a template from its review (the templates area) to exist first; the combiner should set dependsOn on those rows, and may fold these criteria into those areas' rows if they change the shared save controls for every page at once.

increments.title: Back links follow the context a page was opened in
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 builds every journey page's Back link from how the page was reached: to the overview from an overview task, to the template's review page from a template review, and otherwise to the previous page in the step order, including when the page was opened from the review page's Change link. Today task pages point Back at the overview whatever context they were opened in.
acceptanceCriteria: A page opened from its overview task has a 'Back' link to the overview. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498)

A page reached by 'Save and continue' in the opening run has a 'Back' link to the previous page in the step order: 'Main reason for import' goes back to 'What are you importing?', and 'Commodity details' goes back to 'Main reason for import'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498, app/routes.js:1495-1501)

A page opened from a Change link on the review page has a 'Back' link to the previous page in the step order, not to the review page; 'Save and continue' there still returns to the review page. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498)
A page opened from a template's review page has a 'Back' link to that template's review page. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498)
notes: One slice (req-1616, c-206). Depends on the opening-run step-order row (the previous page is taken from the new order) and on the templates area's row that lets a template be edited from its review page (req-1358): the template-review criterion cannot be observed before that context exists, and a requirement cannot be split across rows. Pages behind 'Roles and addresses' (party pickers, CPH number) keep their Back link to it (repo-tests-p2-042), which is not a journey step.

increments.title: Germinal products notifications on their own list and cards
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 lists germinal products notifications only on the germinal products list, counts them in packages and names the commodity by species and product type. No service creates a germinal products notification yet and this programme covers the live-animals journey, so this waits until that journey exists and its notifications reach the INS read model (as the germinal products home section does).
acceptanceCriteria: A germinal products notification appears on the germinal products list and never on the live animals list. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-015, prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-017)

A germinal products notification's card shows its quantity as 'Number of packages', from the notification's package count. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-058; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-082; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-064)

A germinal products notification's card names the commodity as the species then the product type, separated by a comma, such as 'Cattle, Semen'. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-083; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-063)
openQuestions: Blocked: a germinal products notification journey and its dashboard must exist, with its notifications reaching the INS read model; no service builds one today and this programme covers the live-animals journey (as req-979). Who: the programme owner must commission that journey before this row can build.
notes: Drafted by the combiner: req-1736, req-1737 and req-1738 are the germinal products halves the reconciler split out of req-1093, req-1074 and req-1078, all with req-979's blocker. Kept apart from the card and list rows so they build now. Once the journey exists, this row extends the read model's category and quantity and the card's commodity name.
